items.title: EXCLUSIVE: IAIRO Founding Director Prof. Amit Sheth on Building Sovereign "Small AI" for India
items.summary:
In 2017, Google Brain published "Attention Is All You Need," introducing the transformer architecture that powers every major LLM today. While India ranks second globally in AI research paper volume right behind China, its citation influence, the measure of real-world scientific impact—drops to fourth place. Rather than competing in the multi-billion-dollar race to build massive generic foundation models, India’s real opportunity lies in domain-specific, neuro-symbolic "Small AI" tailored to solving localized enterprise, healthcare, and industrial challenges.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Prof. Amit Sheth, Founding Director of IAIRO (Indian AI Research Organization), to break down why India must shift from chasing western "Big AI" to domain-focused "Small AI," how IAIRO's "Sandwich Platform" is dramatically lowering model development costs for startups, the systemic changes needed in academic research funding under ANRF, and how India can build a sustainable "Gurukul" research ecosystem that retains world-class talent.

Can India create foundational breakthroughs by mastering frugal, domain-specific AI?

items.title: India's ₹1.27 Lakh Crore Bet On Semiconductors: Can It Pay Off?
items.summary:
India has moved from semiconductor ambitions to physical execution with the Union Cabinet approving Semicon 2.0 with an outlay of ₹1.27 lakh crore. While Phase 1 saw 12 manufacturing projects worth ₹1.64 lakh crore approved and facilities like Micron, Kaynes Semicon, and CG Semi entering commercial production, building a fab is vastly different from running one profitably. The central question of Semicon 2.0 is whether these individual projects can integrate into a globally competitive, self-sustaining ecosystem or remain dependent on foreign IP and overseas supply chains.

In this episode of Point Break, Antara Gupta sits down with Navin Bishnoi, Chairperson of the Executive Council at IESA (India Electronics and Semiconductor Association), to break down what sets Semicon 2.0 apart, the realistic timeline for commercial silicon fabs like Tata PSMC in Dholera, the pivot toward advanced packaging and compound semiconductors, solving the domestic demand gap, and turning India's massive chip design talent into indigenous IP ownership.

Will India build a truly self-reliant semiconductor industry or remain an assembly hub?

items.title: Jack Dorsey Launches Free Slack But For AI Agents
items.summary:
Jack Dorsey’s company, Block, recently launched Buzz. It's basically a Slack workspace but for AI agents, and it's currently free, decentralized and open-source.

Here's how it works:
👋 It starts you off with a core team: Fizz (the builder), Honey (the writer), and Bumble (the researcher).
💻 You can give them parallel tasks and watch them build it in real time using any model you choose.
✍️ You can even tag them in a thread to peer-review each other's code and offer constructive feedback.
🔒 Because it's built on the open-source Nostr protocol, it's model-agnostic, decentralized, and entirely under your control.

This kind of alternative is great for developers, startups, and anyone looking to run a self-sovereign AI workforce under their own control.

Would this replace Slack for you?

Imagine deploying a Vision-Language-Action (VLA) agent into a high-dimensional Formula 1 racetrack, only to watch it endlessly careen into a fatal phase-space attractor because its parametric weights are strictly frozen. 

To prevent these catastrophic limit cycles without backpropagating a single gradient through the driver's brain, we deploy an exogenous, GRPO-trained 9B meta-controller: the Harness-R1 Telemetry Pit Boss.

Sitting entirely outside the target model's inference engine, this asynchronous orchestrator dynamically rewrites the vehicle’s Markov Decision Process at four exact middleware boundaries. 

By compiling raw environment telemetry into structural Python patches, it injects "on_init" topological priors, steers attention manifolds via "make_pre_hint" state vectors, physically zeroes out the probability mass of fatal action-tensors with an "on_before_action" override, and computes stochastic error-recovery via "on_post_step". 

Optimized strictly against the transductive reward delta (ΔB) of the race batch using a token-averaged, clipped surrogate objective 𝒥(θ), this isn't prompt engineering: it is the rigorous, closed-loop installation of non-differentiable geometric guardrails. 

Maybe the ultimate paradox of modern AI is: you don't need to change the neural network's Hamiltonian to achieve peak autonomy, you just have to relentlessly hack the software boundary conditions (in a synthetic mathematical space) that contain it.

items.title: Why India Doesn't Have Its Own Andrej Karpathy
items.summary:
Andrej Karpathy, Stanford PhD, OpenAI co-founder, former Tesla Autopilot lead, and current pre-training research lead at Anthropic, represents a rare fusion of technical depth, engineering leadership, educator reach, and industry-shaping cultural influence. While India ranks first globally in AI skill penetration and second in GitHub activity, the country holds just 23% of global AI patents compared to China’s 60%.

In this episode of Front Page, Sudhi Sachdev sits down with Mohit Pandey, Senior Tech Journalist at AIM, to break down why India’s tech ecosystem struggles to cultivate and retain world-class research figures, the systemic lack of patient capital for fundamental R&D, why academic paper publishing lacks real-world impact, and how Indian AI culture can shift from corporate job security to celebrating high-risk engineering research.

Can India build and keep its own frontier AI pioneers, or will top talent always flee to western labs?
